title: Embedding priority-bucket smoothing and kernel affinity plan
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Our embeddings endpoint p99 for mixed short+long requests exhibits high tail variance under bursty ingress from web traffic and reranking workloads. Recent investigations show two dominant contributors: (1) micro-batch head-of-line blocking caused by coarse batching windows and contention between low-latency short requests and long-sequence requests; (2) suboptimal kernel scheduling where long-context kernels evict cache residency and increase KV cache stalls for co-located short requests.

Goal: Reduce embedding endpoint p99 by 40-60% for the mixed workload while keeping p50 within 10% of baseline and not increasing overall GPU token cost by more than 5%. Secondary goals: provide deterministic knobs for tenant-priority, expose kernel-affinity telemetry, and create an automated synthetic-burst test harness for CI perf regression monitoring.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for the mixed production trace reduced from baseline (~420ms) to <= 180ms for the target tenant mix
GPU token cost delta <= +5% measured on 72h perf job
end-to-end e2e synthetic burst test added to perf CI with pass/fail thresholds
kernel-affinity telemetry surfaced in Console per-endpoint (histogram + top-k kernels)
tasks: Instrument per-request length tagging and introduce three priority buckets (short, medium, long)
Implement soft-deadline ingress shaper to preferentially dispatch short-bucket requests within micro-batch windows
Add kernel affinity metadata and prefer pinning short-bucket work to low-residency kernels
Tune microbatch windowing heuristics: reduce short bucket window to 2ms, medium 6ms, long 20ms (initial values)
Add speculative hedging for stray long-job stragglers (hedge to quantized variant after 75th percentile on queue wait)
Create synthetic-burst harness that replays production arrival curves and validates pXs
Run 72h stability job across three instance types and capture token cost breakdown
Add rollback flag and runtime feature toggle with metrics gating
notes: 2026-02-22: Spike experiment showed that isolating short requests into a dedicated microbatch path reduced p99 for shorts from 180ms->60ms but increased long-request p99 by ~10% (due to less packing).
2026-02-26: Kernel telemetry added. Observed that long-request kernels (attention with long KV residency) increase L2/L3 thrashing causing short requests to stall when co-located on same GPU stream.
2026-03-02: Draft implementation for priority buckets merged to feature branch. Short window set to 2ms reduced head-of-line by ~55% in local replay.
2026-03-04: Initial kernel-affinity prototype (pin short-bucket to fast-fpath kernels) reduced mixed-workload p99 by 30% in synthetic burst test; GPU utilization remained stable.
2026-03-07: Discovered edge-case where tenant-aware batching plus priority buckets caused starvation in extremely skewed tenant load; added soft fairness backpressure to prevent starvation.

2026-03-10: Run on canary fleet (10 nodes) started. Observed p99 reduction of ~45% for target tenants; logging shows kernel-affinity hints were respected 98% of the time. Still seeing occasional 300ms spikes correlated with GC pauses in runtime sidecar. Tracking separately with ENG-843210.
decision_log: 2026-02-24: Decision to use three priority buckets (short/medium/long) instead of continuous priority to keep scheduler complexity manageable (agreed by Rafael, Priya, and Lina).
2026-03-01: Chose kernel-affinity hints (soft pin) rather than hard pin to avoid reducing scheduler flexibility during autoscale events.
2026-03-06: Opted for speculative hedging to quantized model variant after queue wait threshold instead of immediate fallback to preserve quality for most requests.
perf_results: Baseline (prod mixed trace): p50=22ms, p95=120ms, p99=420ms, GPU token cost=1.00x
Local replay (priority-bucket + short-window): p99=250ms (-40%), p50=25ms (+14%), token cost=1.03x
Synthetic-burst (kernel-affinity prototype): p99=230ms (-45%), p50=24ms (+9%), kernel-affinity respected=98%
Canary 10-node run (72h, mixed tenants): p99=230ms (-45%), observed sporadic GC spikes causing rare 300ms events (investigating)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Short-bucket aggressive windows could increase overall token cost due to less packing. Mitigation: CI cost check and dynamic window expansion under low load.
Risk: Kernel pinning reduces packing efficiency across tenants during autoscale. Mitigation: use soft hints with eviction policy and autoscaler-aware relaxation.
Risk: Starvation for long-bucket under skew. Mitigation: implement fairness tokens and age-based promotion out of priority buckets.
Risk: Regression in embedding quality due to speculative hedges. Mitigation: run hedged requests against unhedged baseline in shadow mode for 48h and track embedding similarity regression alerts.
rollback_plan: Feature toggle at ingress -> disable priority-buckets and kernel-affinity hints. Revert microbatch windowing via runtime flag. If token cost delta > +8% or p99 > baseline for >2h, toggle off and rollback PRs in runtime repo.
next_steps: Complete canary run and validate 72h token cost and quality shadowing
Address GC spike sources with ENG-843210 and re-run canary if necessary
Prepare runtime-1.20 release notes and Console dashboard widgets for kernel-affinity histograms
Schedule PM/Eng review on 2026-03-16 to decide wider rollout
